note: Re-judged 2026-11-20 by an independent agent after 06bd727362 changed the negative TestSPDPolicyEqualOrderOnOverlapRefused. RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1: "Thus, a user or administrator MUST be able to order the entries to express a desired access control policy." The change is mechanical: orderTotalPeer lost its priority parameter and fixes policy-priority 2000 inside the helper, and every call passed 2000 before, so each case has the same peers, selectors and VTI binding, and no assertion changed. The test still drives verifySPDOrder: overlapping operator entries at one order, and an entry at an overlapping peer's policy-priority, are refused with the operator error naming both entries, the shared order and the exact fix; overlapping entries at distinct orders, disjoint entries at one order and an entry beside a peer bound to an XFRM interface are accepted. The positive TestSpdOperatorOrdersOverlappingPeers (both directions installed at ranks 500 and 1500, in that order) and the negative TestSpdUnstatedOrderTakesTheDefaultRank are unchanged. The negative's discrimination record was re-taken in 06bd727362. Verdict stands.
